Everyone in the comments seems to question why Ashar having concerns regarding Khirad and Khijar. Everyone's saying that it's hypocritical of him cause he himself has a female friend. Which is fair, I am not gonna dismiss this argument. It has its ground. But I would like to add somethings. I think his problem isn't Khirad having a male friend, it's khizar's behavior that is bothering him and the fact that Khirad is not understanding or overlooking khizar's behavior or she's just thinking that khizar is being friendly. Which is again not her fault completely. The main culprit here is Khizar here. Ashar's concerns are regarding him and the way he's crossing boundaries, which is not right! And the fact that Khirad is a simplistic girl, as the show heavily implies that she's a masoom and very kind hearted woman. Which is totally fine and not wrong at all! But people tend to take advantage of such people, use them, exploit them in a way that ruin their life, family, relationships everything etc.! And Ashar's concern gains more ground as he is constantly heard from his father, mother, people around him and he also genuinely believes that Khirad is a masoom and kind hearted woman! Again which is not wrong to be masoom and kind hearted, but his concerns is that her this masoomiyat and kind heartiness is not letting her see through the actual motives and intentions of Khizar! And he is concern that khizar might use Khirad! Which can lead up to catastrophic consequences. It might not always be the case that a man doesn't trust his wife, but the fact that he as man knows what other man are like! Which some women might fail to see behind all the sweet impressions and stuffs! So his concerns are genuinely valid, please try to understand this. And regarding the hypocrisy part, yes he himself had female friend, but there are somethings to clear up! First of all I am a firm believer on the fact that a man and a woman cannot ever be just friends, one will always want to be more than that. And it's the case of majority! So in my framework both are wrong here to keep male/female friends or even interact with opposite gender frankly or in a way that might give the other person wrong impression. Sure your intentions were clear, but the other person's interpretation of your intentions might not be! So in my personal opinion and framework, both Ashar and Khirad are wrong to keep friends of opposite gender respectively. Even tho Khirad is not keeping khizar as her friend, but he heavily insists on that, which is his problem as I said earlier about intentions and interpretation. Khirad is just being a nice person where as khizar is interpreting it in a wrong way! Again which is his problem. So Khirad is really has the edge when it comes to who is closer to being right. I am insisting on these points to clear up that I am not here to take sides, not Ashar's nor Khirad. And I am here also not to justify any wrong behavior of Ashar, I am just trying give valid reasons and concerns why as of this point in the series Ashar is concerned. So now I will talk outside of my framework, so regarding Ashar and Sara's friendship we have to understand that their friendship is long before Ashar and Khirad's marriage. They're childhood friends! Their friendship really has a much more strong ground than Khirad and khizar's! Ashar just can't suddenly stop being friends with Sara out of nowhere! So saying that Ashar is a hypocrite purely based on this criteria that he's friends with Sara is not completely justified imo if we keep my own framework outside and talk from a different,more liberal perspective. And one other thing is that Khirad's constant mention of Khizar in front of Ashar. Which is not right, we didn't see Ashar doing that around with Khirad, constantly mentioning Sara. Khirad maybe doing this unknowingly but it's still doesn't sit right with him, in fact it will not with any spouse respectively! And the other thing is Khizar's constant involvement in Khirad's life and his family which is affecting himself! And his relationship with Khirad! His unusual interest in Khirad's life, coming out of nowhere in their house, being so frank with Khirad doesn't sit right with him! On top of that when Khirad keeps bringing khizar into conversation it really bother's him. Yes he should confront khizar about all these and this is where I will say he's wrong! Instead of confronting the actual culprit he shouldn't make assumptions that can lead up to something horrible! And this is a legit criticism! And we should talk about tthis! Not just outright call him hypocrite and judge all men cause of this! But Khirad also should understand that it is bothering him, as she her says that wo Khud ko Ashar k dhatch me dhal na chahti hai! You don't have to be Sherlock Holmes to figure this out. [Edit:one other thing I would like to add is that Ashar should have cleared up what was bothering him and also Khirad should have also asked if he's mad with him,yes she did asked at the tie scene but she should have asked if this specific thing is bothering him(khizar's unusual interest in Khirad's life)].But again I am not putting all the blame on Khirad as well as Ashar, that will be unjustified. One other thing tho that Ashar should clearly say that what's bothering him. That is another legit point of criticism that why just he doesn't say what is his problem instead of making up assumptions. So yeah thats all I have to say Ig.

I feel the director was showing that despite everything that had happened, Khirad still had that instinctive love and care for Ashar. But then, as the discussion continues, you can see that love being buried beneath all the hurt and hatred she now carries for him.

That contrast is what makes the scene so powerful. The actors didn’t need to explain what the characters were feeling. Their expressions did it all.

When I first started watching Humsafar, I thought Ashar, Farida—everyone was genuinely good. I actually thought Farida was such a loving and caring mother-in-law. I kept wondering, “Can something really happen in a drama that will make the heroine suffer this much? Will Ashar and Khirad actually separate?”

I never imagined that Farida had been planning everything from the very beginning. She hated Khirad from the start but never let anyone understand what she really felt. Her acting was so convincing. Later, she teamed up with Zarina and Khizr and created a whole conspiracy to make Khirad look bad in front of Ashar.

What kind of mother does that to her own son? She literally destroyed her own son's life. Everything was going perfectly until Farida ruined it all. If she hadn't done what she did, Sara would probably have gotten married by now instead of waiting all those years for Ashar. And in the end, Sara died. She didn't have to die either. 😭

Ashar is actually a good man. He trusted his mother, and honestly, how could he ever imagine that his own mother was capable of doing something like this? Yes, he was wrong for not believing Khirad, but he loved her so deeply. 💔

And honestly, I'm glad Farida went crazy in the end. She deserved it after everything she did. 😭

Asher probably never knew failure in his life. As a rich, good-looking kid, things likely came easily to him. He was content as long as he remained the center of Khirad’s world. When she began studying and building a life beyond him, he seemed to grow insecure. His mother noticed this and later exploited it to drive a wedge between them.

His shock at finding Khirad in a compromising situation with another man is understandable, but his reaction was absolutely not. He knew Khirad was principled and brutally honest, so why he didn’t even give her a chance to explain is something I’ll never understand. What makes it worse is that he was perceptive enough to see through Sara’s fake kindness and even call it out. Yet with Khirad - the woman he claimed to love - he showed no such discernment. His wounded ego and fear of humiliation completely blinded him.

None of this justifies the injustice he inflicted on Khirad. His real punishment is having to live with the knowledge that he failed both his wife and daughter. Even if they move forward, neither of them will ever forget these four years. Khirad returned only because of their child, and while they may build a life together again, I feel the essence of their relationship was permanently lost.
